points.description: States that a static array persists (has static storage duration) for the entire life/lifetime of the program, rather than only during the function call, using terms such as 'static' and 'life of the program'.
points.partial_credit: 1 mark if it says static arrays persist/retain values between calls but does not state lifetime is the whole program.

points.description: States that a static array is initialized only once, the first time the function that declares it is called (not on each call).
points.partial_credit: 1 mark if it says initialized only once but omits that this happens at the first call of the declaring function.

points.description: Correctly contrasts with a non-static (automatic/local) array: it is created and initialized on each call of the function and destroyed when the function exits, so it does not live for the whole program.

rubric.notes: Full marks need precise statements: static array lives for the whole program, is initialized only once on the first call of its function, and the non-static array differs (re-created each call, destroyed on exit). Vague statements like 'static arrays keep their value' earn at most part of P1. Any wrong statement about a point (e.g. static arrays are re-initialized each call, or static means constant size) means that point earns nothing.
